ordered_diagnoses: Sjögren's Syndrome with Central Nervous System Involvement

s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of neurological deficits with evidence of inflammation and white matter changes
salient_findings: Mild aphasia and confusion
Sudden-onset right leg weakness
Mild headache and right facial droop
Extensive white matter changes on MRI
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level
key_facts: History of well-controlled hypertension and hyperlipidemia
On methotrexate and sulfasalazine treatment
Developed mild aphasia and confusion lasting for several hours
Right leg weakness resolved within 2 days
Presented with mild headache and right facial droop
Neurological examination revealed paraphasic errors and word-finding difficulty
Mild right nasolabial flattening and bilateral upgoing plantars
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level
High titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody
CSF analysis showed 12/µL white blood cell count and 4 oligoclonal bands
MRI Brain showed extensive white matter changes with enhancement along the arachnoid surface

shortlist: Sjögren's Syndrome with Central Nervous System Involvement

shortlist.label: Multiple Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of neurological deficits with evidence of inflammation and white matter changes, CSF analysis showed 4 oligoclonal bands

shortlist.label: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
shortlist.why_kept: History of optic neuritis and transverse myelitis not explicitly mentioned but high titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody and CSF analysis showed 12/µL white blood cell count

shortlist.label: Primary Central Nervous System Vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: MRI Brain showed extensive white matter changes with enhancement along the arachnoid surface, no evidence of vasculitis on pathological tests but clinical presentation suggests inflammation

shortlist.label: Sjögren's Syndrome with Central Nervous System Involvement
shortlist.why_kept: High titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, history of well-controlled hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and neurological examination revealed paraphasic errors and word-finding difficulty

shortlist.label: Susac Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of neurological deficits, history of mild aphasia and confusion, and MRI Brain showed extensive white matter changes

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of relapsing neurological symptoms, such as mild aphasia, confusion, right leg weakness, and right facial droop, along with the presence of oligoclonal bands in the CSF and extensive white matter changes on MRI, are characteristic of Multiple Sclerosis. The high titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody may also be seen in MS.

rejected.label: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
rejected.why: The absence of optic neuritis and spinal cord involvement makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Primary Central Nervous System Vasculitis
rejected.why: The brain biopsy did not show evidence of vasculitis, and the MRI did not reveal any vascular abnormalities.

rejected.label: Sjögren's Syndrome with Central Nervous System Involvement
rejected.why: There is no mention of symptoms or laboratory findings typical of Sjögren's Syndrome, such as dry eyes or mouth, or positive anti-SSA/Ro or anti-SSB/La antibodies.

rejected.label: Susac Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and imaging findings do not match the characteristic clinical triad of Susac Syndrome, which includes encephalopathy, branch retinal artery occlusions, and hearing loss.
